court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: RLUIPA substantial burden
issues.why: Court must decide whether denial of Ramadan-compliant OJKD substantially burdened Roberts’s sincere religious exercise.

issues.label: RLUIPA sincere belief
issues.why: Court must confirm sincerity is undisputed and thus not a basis for denying protection.

issues.label: RLUIPA compelling interest
issues.why: If burden exists, court must assess whether food safety/logistics constitute a compelling governmental interest.

issues.label: RLUIPA least restrictive means
issues.why: Court must decide whether offering only Common Fare/stop fasting was the least restrictive means versus feasible alternatives.

issues.label: RLUIPA individual-capacity liability
issues.why: Court must address whether RLUIPA authorizes suits against officials in individual capacities at all.

issues.label: RLUIPA official-capacity relief
issues.why: Court must determine what prospective relief is available against officials in official capacities under RLUIPA.

issues.label: RLUIPA money damages bar
issues.why: Court must apply precedent barring RLUIPA monetary damages against states/officials.

issues.label: RLUIPA declaratory relief scope
issues.why: Court must decide whether declaratory relief is still live or barred by mootness/sovereign immunity limits.

issues.label: Mootness of injunctive claims
issues.why: Court must determine whether the 2021 Ramadan-compliant OJKD moots prospective relief requests.

issues.label: Voluntary cessation exception
issues.why: Court must assess whether VDOC’s policy change could be reversed, keeping claims for injunction alive.

issues.label: Capable-of-repetition exception
issues.why: Court must evaluate whether Ramadan’s recurring nature and VDOC discretion make recurrence likely yet time-limited.

issues.label: Effect of prisoner’s transfers
issues.why: Court must consider whether transfer risk or continued confinement at Red Onion affects mootness.

issues.label: Standing and redressability
issues.why: Court must ensure each form of relief would redress a current or past injury and is not advisory.

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment immunity
issues.why: Court must apply sovereign immunity to damages claims against officials in official capacities.

issues.label: Ex parte Young applicability
issues.why: Court must determine whether prospective injunctive/declaratory relief can proceed against current officials.

issues.label: Proper defendant substitution
issues.why: Court must confirm substitution of Walters for Clarke for prospective relief and its jurisdictional effects.

issues.label: PLRA limits on injunctions
issues.why: Court must ensure any prospective relief is narrowly drawn and least intrusive under the PLRA.

issues.label: PLRA physical-injury rule
issues.why: Court must consider whether compensatory damages for mental/emotional injury are barred absent physical injury, despite food-poisoning evidence.

issues.label: PLRA exhaustion
issues.why: Court must determine whether Roberts exhausted available administrative remedies for each claim and defendant.

issues.label: Exhaustion scope and timing
issues.why: Court must decide whether grievances covered Ramadan/OJKD specifics and whether deadlines/availability excused noncompliance.

issues.label: Personal involvement of defendants
issues.why: For §1983 damages, court must decide each defendant’s personal participation or causal connection to the denial.

issues.label: Supervisory liability limits
issues.why: Court must apply limits on respondeat superior and decide if supervisors had knowledge and deliberate indifference/causation.

issues.label: Causation and damages proof
issues.why: Court must decide if the denial caused Roberts’s illness and other damages versus his decision to store food.

issues.label: Mitigation and comparative fault
issues.why: Court must consider whether Roberts’s self-help storage of meals affects causation or damages.

issues.label: Free Exercise threshold burden
issues.why: Court must determine whether the policy imposed a substantial burden on religious exercise under the First Amendment.

issues.label: Turner reasonableness test
issues.why: Court must apply Turner factors to prison regulation/decision impacting religious practice.

issues.label: Penological interests evidence
issues.why: Court must assess adequacy of evidence on safety, cost, staffing, timing, and ordering constraints supporting denial.

issues.label: Availability of alternatives
issues.why: Under Turner/RLUIPA, court must consider less burdensome alternatives like prepackaging, timing changes, or temporary exceptions.

issues.label: Discrimination vs neutrality
issues.why: Court must decide whether the denial reflected neutral, generally applicable policy or targeted religion-based discrimination.

issues.label: Sincere belief scope limits
issues.why: Court must decide whether Free Exercise protects Roberts’s idiosyncratic belief equating Kashrut supervision with Islamic law.

issues.label: Qualified immunity framework
issues.why: Court must decide whether a constitutional violation occurred and whether clearly established law put defendants on notice.

issues.label: Clearly established Free Exercise right
issues.why: Court must determine whether it was clearly established that officials must accommodate Ramadan fasting while on a stringent kosher-supervised diet.

issues.label: Clearly established specificity level
issues.why: Court must choose the proper level of generality for defining the right in the qualified-immunity analysis.

issues.label: Objective reasonableness
issues.why: Court must decide whether reasonable officials could believe their options offered were lawful given constraints.

issues.label: Equal Protection comparator choice
issues.why: Court must identify proper comparators (Jewish OJKD inmates, Muslim Common Fare fasters, others) for differential treatment analysis.

issues.label: Equal Protection intent requirement
issues.why: Court must determine whether Roberts proved intentional discrimination, not just disparate impact.

issues.label: Equal Protection level of scrutiny
issues.why: Court must decide whether strict scrutiny applies (religion) or rational-basis/Turner-type deference governs in prison context.

issues.label: Equal Protection legitimate reasons
issues.why: Court must assess whether safety and administrative reasons justify any disparate treatment.

issues.label: Establishment Clause theory
issues.why: Court must clarify whether accommodating Jewish dietary needs but not Roberts’s request constitutes endorsement/denomination preference.

issues.label: Establishment Clause standard
issues.why: Court must select governing test (e.g., coercion, endorsement, neutrality) and apply in prison-accommodation context.

issues.label: Denominational preference issue
issues.why: Court must decide whether the OJKD program creates impermissible preference for Judaism over Islam or is neutral accommodation.

issues.label: Free Exercise vs Establishment balance
issues.why: Court must consider whether denying Roberts was justified by avoiding Establishment problems or whether accommodation is permissible.

issues.label: Declaratory relief justiciability
issues.why: Court must decide if retrospective declarations about 2020 conduct are permissible or moot/impermissibly advisory.

issues.label: State-law or policy relevance
issues.why: Court must consider how VDOC manuals/policies inform reasonableness, notice, and feasibility without creating federal rights.

issues.label: Discovery ruling reviewability
issues.why: Court must decide whether denial of motion to compel affected summary-judgment fairness and warrants reversal/remand.

issues.label: Summary-judgment record adequacy
issues.why: Court must ensure disputes of material fact (feasibility, timing, safety, notice) are properly resolved in nonmovant’s favor.

issues.label: Remedies against individuals
issues.why: Court must determine availability and standards for compensatory and punitive damages under §1983.

issues.label: Punitive damages standard
issues.why: Court must decide whether evidence shows evil motive or reckless indifference to federally protected rights.

issues.label: Nominal damages availability
issues.why: Court must consider whether nominal damages remain available for completed constitutional violations even if other relief is moot.

issues.label: Statute of limitations
issues.why: Court must verify claims arising from 2020 events are timely under applicable limitations period and accrual rules.

issues.label: Relation back of amendment
issues.why: Court must decide whether the 2021 amended complaint adding Establishment claim relates back and is timely.

issues.label: Proper capacity pleadings
issues.why: Court must ensure claims are correctly analyzed by capacity (official vs individual) for immunity and remedies.

issues.label: Injunctive relief specificity
issues.why: Court must decide whether requested injunction is sufficiently specific and enforceable, especially given updated 2021 policy.
